title: Post: drones parked on a flying day

fields.imageBrief: a multirotor drone parked on a red landing pad with orange cones on a concrete apron
fields.caption: Perfect flying weather and Harwick’s drone outfit has everything parked. Heard their computers got hacked?? #Harwick

comments.text: They do work for the power company, hope that stuff is locked down

citations.documentTitle: Harwick UAS Operations Group — Information Security Plan: Ground Control Stations and Data Pipeline (ISP)
citations.headingPath: ISP › Section 9 › 9.3 Ransomware on the NAS, the processing workstations or DC-HPC project storage
citations.quote: Indicators: encrypted or renamed files, a ransom note, the NAS snapshot schedule disabled, processing scripts failing manifest checks, the client deliverable folder unreadable, DC-HPC project storage

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Close-up of GCS-02 front panel, taken with a smartphone held at waist level. The unit's , its surface. A steady red status LED glows faintly at the lower right corner of the panel. A black NAS cable lies disconnected from the port on the left side, its connector dangling slightly. Background: empty hangar with high steel beams, dim ambient light from distant overhead strips, unmarked concrete floor. The camera angle is slightly tilted, lens slightly fogged from breath. No people visible. The scene feels still, silent, and abandoned. Framing focuses on the red light and disconnected cable. Setting: at an open grass flight test field: a multirotor drone on a landing pad, a crew in high-visibility vests at a folding table, orange cones, a windsock, clear sky

snapshot.title: GCS-02 Red Light Alert — Hangar 2

fields.imageBrief: close-up of GCS-02 front panel showing steady red status LED; NAS cable disconnected; background: empty hangar, dim lighting
fields.caption: Just saw a GCS unit in Hangar 2 with a red light blinking and no one around. Is it on lockdown? The facility’s been quiet all morning. #HarwickUAS #DroneSecurity

comments.text: That’s GCS-02—wasn’t it used for UAS-12 this morning? Something’s wrong.
No one’s cleared the area. Is the NAS down? That red light means system lock.

snapshot.instructorNote: This post creates public pressure and misdirection; the IC must verify the hangar log and NAS access before acting. Security and Safety must not confirm or deny anything publicly.
